test.name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties - Test 1

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following chlorides has the highest covalent character?

text_solutions: Covalent character increases with higher charge and smaller cation size (Fajans’ rule). \(\ce{BeCl2}\) (Be²⁺, small) has the highest covalent character among group 2 chlorides.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the general outer electronic configuration of f-block elements?

text_solutions: f-block elements (lanthanoids and actinoids) fill \((n-2)f\) orbitals, with a general outer configuration of \((n-2)f^{1-14} (n-1)d^{0-1} ns^2\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 17 element forms a hydride with the highest dipole moment?

text_solutions: Dipole moment depends on electronegativity difference and bond length. \(\ce{HF}\) (F, highest electronegativity, shortest bond) has the highest dipole moment among HF, HCl, HBr, and HI.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the ground state electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^1\)?

text_solutions: This configuration (Z=31) corresponds to Ga (period 4, group 13), with \(4p^1\) distinguishing it from Zn (\(4p^0\)), Ge (\(4p^2\)), or As (\(4p^3\)).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 16 element forms the most stable dioxide at room temperature?

text_solutions: Group 16 dioxides vary in stability. \(\ce{SO2}\) (bent, gaseous) is the most stable at room temperature due to strong S=O bonds, unlike \(\ce{O2}\) (diatomic gas), \(\ce{SeO2}\) (polymeric solid), or \(\ce{TeO2}\) (solid).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the compound formed by carbon and chlorine?

text_solutions: C (group 14, valence 4) and Cl (group 17, valence 1) form \(\ce{CCl4}\) by sharing electrons to achieve stable configurations.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide of a group 13 element is amphoteric and used in the extraction of aluminium?

text_solutions: Among group 13 oxides, \(\ce{Al2O3}\) is amphoteric and is the ore (bauxite) used in aluminium extraction, unlike \(\ce{B2O3}\) (acidic), \(\ce{Ga2O3}\), or \(\ce{In2O3}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the highest density among the alkali metals?

text_solutions: Density generally increases down group 1 due to increasing atomic mass, with Cs having the highest density among Li, Na, K, and Cs.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 14 has the highest electronegativity?

text_solutions: Electronegativity decreases down a group. Among C, Si, Ge, and Pb (group 14), C (period 2) has the highest value.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the temporary systematic name of the element with atomic number 118?

text_solutions: For \(Z=118\): 1 (un), 1 (un), 8 (oct) → ununoctium (before being named Oganesson).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the highest melting point among the alkali metals?

text_solutions: Among alkali metals (group 1), melting point decreases down the group due to weaker metallic bonding with increasing size. Li, being smallest, has the highest melting point.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which d-block element in the fourth period has the highest first ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: In period 4 d-block (Sc to Zn), ionization enthalpy increases across due to increasing nuclear charge, with Zn (\(3d^{10} 4s^2\)) having the highest due to its full d-subshell stability.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which pair of elements from different periods shows the greatest similarity in oxide acidity?

text_solutions: Diagonal relationships lead to similar oxide properties. C (period 2) and Si (period 3) both form acidic oxides (\(\ce{CO2}\), \(\ce{SiO2}\)) with covalent character, unlike other pairs.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the systematic element name for the element with atomic number 117 before its official naming?

text_solutions: For \(Z=117\): 1 (un), 1 (un), 7 (sept) → ununseptium (before being named Tennessine).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 17 has the highest tendency to form ionic compounds with group 1 elements?

text_solutions: Ionic character increases with larger electronegativity difference. F (highest electronegativity, 4.0) forms the most ionic compounds with group 1 elements (e.g., \(\ce{NaF}\)) compared to Cl, Br, or I.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 17 shows an anomaly in electron gain enthalpy compared to its neighbors?

text_solutions: F has less negative electron gain enthalpy than Cl due to electron repulsion in its compact 2p orbitals, an anomaly in group 17 trends where Cl > Br > I.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the largest ionic radius among group 17 anions?

text_solutions: Ionic radius increases down group 17. Among \(\ce{F^-}\), \(\ce{Cl^-}\), \(\ce{Br^-}\), and \(\ce{I^-}\), \(\ce{I^-}\) (from I, period 5) has the largest radius.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 1 has the lowest second ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Second ionization enthalpy for group 1 elements involves removing an electron from \(\ce{X+}\) (noble gas configuration). Cs⁺ (largest size) has the lowest value due to reduced nuclear attraction.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 2 has the highest hydration energy in its ionic form?

text_solutions: Hydration energy increases with smaller cation size and higher charge density. Be²⁺ (smallest) has the highest hydration energy among Be, Mg, Ca, and Sr.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 14 has the lowest melting point?

text_solutions: Melting point in group 14 decreases from C (covalent network) to Sn and Pb (metallic), with Sn having the lowest among C, Si, Ge, and Sn due to weaker metallic bonding.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which ion among the following isoelectronic species with 36 electrons has the largest radius?

text_solutions: For isoelectronic species (36 electrons), radius increases with decreasing nuclear charge. \(\ce{Br^-}\) (Z=35) has the largest radius compared to \(\ce{K+}\), \(\ce{Ca^2+}\), or \(\ce{Sc^3+}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group contains only p-block elements?

text_solutions: p-block spans groups 13–18. Options: (1) Na (group 1), Mg (group 2) → s-block; (2) B (group 13), C (group 14) → p-block; (3) Li (group 1), Be (group 2) → s-block; (4) K (group 1), Ca (group 2) → s-block.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fifth period has the highest electronegativity among p-block elements?

text_solutions: In period 5 p-block (Rb to Xe), electronegativity increases across. I (group 17) has the highest electronegativity among Sn, Sb, and I, excluding noble gases.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 16 element has the highest tendency to form stable compounds in the +4 oxidation state?

text_solutions: The +4 oxidation state is most stable for S in group 16, forming \(\ce{SO2}\) (gaseous, strong S=O bonds), more stable than \(\ce{O2}\), \(\ce{SeO2}\) (polymeric), or \(\ce{TeO2}\) (solid).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^2\)?

text_solutions: Total electrons = 14, corresponding to Si (period 3, group 14). Others: Al (13 electrons), P (15 electrons), Mg (12 electrons).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 17 element exhibits the least reactivity with hydrogen due to its bond strength?

text_solutions: Reactivity with hydrogen decreases down group 17 as H-X bond strength weakens. F forms the strongest H-F bond, making \(\ce{HF}\) the least reactive among HF, HCl, HBr, and HI.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which ion among the following has the highest effective nuclear charge for an isoelectronic series with 10 electrons?

text_solutions: For isoelectronic species (10 electrons), effective nuclear charge increases with atomic number. \(\ce{Al^3+}\) (Z=13) has the highest effective nuclear charge compared to \(\ce{Na+}\), \(\ce{Mg^2+}\), or \(\ce{F^-}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: The atomic radius of which element is the largest among the following?

text_solutions: Atomic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group. Among F, Cl, Br, and I (group 17), Iodine (I), being lowest in the group, has the largest atomic radius.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fourth period has the highest metallic character?

text_solutions: Metallic character decreases across a period and increases down a group. In period 4, K (group 1) has the highest metallic character compared to Ca, Sc, or Ti.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which pair of elements from different groups shows the closest similarity in ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Diagonal relationships reduce ionization enthalpy differences. Be (group 2, period 2) and Al (group 13, period 3) have similar values due to size and charge effects, unlike other pairs.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the compound formed between silicon and chlorine?

text_solutions: Si (group 14, valence 4) and Cl (group 17, valence 1) form \(\ce{SiCl4}\), a covalent compound, by sharing electrons to complete octets.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the lowest electronegativity?

text_solutions: Electronegativity decreases down a group and increases across a period. Among F, Cl, K, and Cs, Cs (group 1, period 6) has the lowest value.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following shows a diagonal relationship with Li?

text_solutions: Diagonal relationships occur between second and third period elements (e.g., Li and Mg) due to similar size and electronegativity, unlike Na, K, or Be.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the second period has the least tendency to form ionic bonds?

text_solutions: Ionic bonding decreases across a period as electronegativity increases. F (group 17, electronegativity 4.0) prefers covalent bonds, unlike Li, Be, or B.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Arrange the following elements in order of decreasing electron affinity: F, Cl, Br, I.

text_solutions: Electron affinity decreases down group 17, with Cl highest due to optimal size and nuclear charge, followed by F (anomaly due to repulsion). Order: Cl > F > Br > I.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element exhibits a diagonal relationship with carbon?

text_solutions: C (group 14, period 2) has a diagonal relationship with Si (group 14, period 3) due to similar properties, unlike B, N, or P.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements was predicted as Eka-boron by Mendeleev?

text_solutions: Mendeleev predicted Eka-boron below B in group 13, later identified as Ga, with similar properties to B, unlike Sc (group 3), Ge (group 14), or Tc (group 7).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following sulfates has the highest solubility in water due to its hydration energy?

text_solutions: Solubility of group 2 sulfates decreases down the group as hydration energy drops with increasing cation size. \(\ce{BeSO4}\) (smallest cation) has the highest solubility.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 14 has the highest tendency to exhibit catenation?

text_solutions: Catenation (self-linking) is strongest for C due to its small size and strong C-C bond energy, far exceeding Si, Ge, or Sn in group 14.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the general outer electronic configuration of group 2 elements?

text_solutions: Group 2 elements (alkaline earth metals) have 2 valence electrons, with outer configuration \(ns^2\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element exhibits the most negative electron gain enthalpy?

text_solutions: Electron gain enthalpy becomes more negative across a period and less negative down a group. Among O, S, F, and Cl, Cl (group 17, period 3) has the most negative value due to its high effective nuclear charge and smaller size than S.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 1 has the highest reactivity with water?

text_solutions: Reactivity with water increases down group 1 due to decreasing ionization enthalpy. Cs (lowest ionization enthalpy) reacts most vigorously among Li, Na, K, and Cs.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 13 shows the maximum deviation from typical metallic character?

text_solutions: Metallic character increases down group 13. B (period 2) is a metalloid with minimal metallic properties, unlike Al, Ga, or In, which are more metallic.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 2 element has the highest lattice energy in its chloride compound?

text_solutions: Lattice energy increases with smaller cation size and higher charge density. \(\ce{BeCl2}\) (Be²⁺, smallest) has the highest lattice energy among Be, Mg, Ca, and Sr chlorides.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 1 element has the highest ionic conductivity in its molten chloride form?

text_solutions: Ionic conductivity in molten salts increases with smaller cation size due to higher mobility. LiCl has the highest conductivity among Li, Na, K, and Cs chlorides.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 15 forms a pentoxide with the highest thermal stability?

text_solutions: Thermal stability of group 15 pentoxides (\(\ce{X2O5}\)) decreases down the group due to weaker X-O bonds. \(\ce{N2O5}\) is the most stable thermally, decomposing at a higher temperature than \(\ce{P2O5}\), \(\ce{As2O5}\), or \(\ce{Sb2O5}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the second period has the highest electron affinity?

text_solutions: Electron affinity increases across period 2. F has the highest electron affinity in period 2 (Li, Be, N, F), though less than Cl (period 3) due to electron repulsion in its compact 2p orbitals.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 1 element has the highest flame coloration intensity due to its ionization energy?

text_solutions: Flame color intensity increases with lower ionization energy, allowing easier electron excitation. Cs (lowest ionization energy) exhibits the highest intensity among Li, Na, K, and Cs.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^5\)?

text_solutions: Total electrons = 17, corresponding to Cl (period 3, group 17). Others: S (16 electrons), Ar (18 electrons), P (15 electrons).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 16 element forms a dioxide that exists as a linear gas at room temperature?

text_solutions: In group 16, \(\ce{O2}\) is a linear diatomic gas at room temperature, unlike \(\ce{SO2}\) (bent), \(\ce{SeO2}\) (polymeric solid), or \(\ce{TeO2}\) (solid).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the compound formed between phosphorus and oxygen in its highest oxidation state?

text_solutions: P (group 15, valence 5 in +5 state) forms \(\ce{P2O5}\) with oxygen (valence 2), a stable acidic oxide.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the temporary systematic name of the element with atomic number 113?

text_solutions: For \(Z=113\): 1 (un), 1 (un), 3 (tri) → ununtrium (before being named Nihonium).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following nitrates decomposes most readily to form a basic oxide?

text_solutions: Group 2 nitrates decompose to basic oxides, \(\ce{NO2}\), and \(\ce{O2}\). \(\ce{Be(NO3)2}\) decomposes most readily to \(\ce{BeO}\) (basic) due to Be²⁺’s small size and high charge density, which weakens the nitrate lattice.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the compound formed between aluminium and sulfur?

text_solutions: Al (group 13, valence 3) and S (group 16, valence 2) form \(\ce{Al2S3}\) by cross-multiplying valences, a stable ionic compound.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the compound formed between boron and fluorine?

text_solutions: B (group 13, valence 3) and F (group 17, valence 1) form \(\ce{BF3}\), a stable covalent compound, unlike \(\ce{BF}\), \(\ce{BF2}\), or \(\ce{B2F3}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 13 has the lowest third ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Third ionization enthalpy decreases down group 13 as size increases, reducing nuclear attraction. Tl (period 6) has the lowest value among B, Al, Ga, and Tl.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the compound formed between germanium and oxygen?

text_solutions: Ge (group 14, valence 4) forms \(\ce{GeO2}\) with oxygen (valence 2), a stable covalent oxide, unlike \(\ce{GeO}\), \(\ce{Ge2O}\), or \(\ce{GeO4}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 17 has the lowest electron affinity?

text_solutions: Electron affinity decreases down group 17 due to increasing size and reduced nuclear attraction. I (period 5) has the lowest value among F, Cl, Br, and I.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the smallest ionic radius?

text_solutions: For isoelectronic species (\(\ce{O^2-}\), \(\ce{F^-}\), \(\ce{Na+}\), \(\ce{Mg^2+}\), all with 10 electrons), radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge. \(\ce{Mg^2+}\) (Z=12) has the smallest radius.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the ground state electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^6 4s^2\)?

text_solutions: This configuration (Z=26) corresponds to Fe (period 4, group 8), with \(3d^6 4s^2\), distinguishing it from Mn (\(3d^5 4s^2\)), Co (\(3d^7 4s^2\)), or Ni (\(3d^8 4s^2\)).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 2 has the highest hydration enthalpy due to its ionic size?

text_solutions: Hydration enthalpy increases with smaller ionic size and higher charge density. Be²⁺ (smallest in group 2) has the highest hydration enthalpy compared to Mg²⁺, Ca²⁺, or Sr²⁺.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the compound formed by magnesium and nitrogen?

text_solutions: Mg (group 2, valence 2) and N (group 15, valence 3) form \(\ce{Mg3N2}\) by cross-multiplying valences.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the lowest first ionization enthalpy in the fifth period?

text_solutions: First ionization enthalpy decreases across a period from right to left. In period 5, Rb (group 1) has the lowest value compared to Sr, Ag, and I.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 13 has the highest ionization enthalpy after losing two electrons?

text_solutions: Third ionization enthalpy is highest for B (removing an electron from \(\ce{B^2+}\) with \(1s^2\)) due to its small size and stable configuration, compared to Al, Ga, or In.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: How many elements are present in the fourth period of the periodic table?

text_solutions: The fourth period (\(n=4\)) includes \(4s\), \(3d\), and \(4p\) orbitals, accommodating 18 electrons, hence 18 elements (K to Kr).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the general outer electronic configuration of group 17 elements?

text_solutions: Group 17 elements (halogens) have 7 valence electrons, with outer configuration \(ns^2 np^5\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements has the highest metallic character?

text_solutions: Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period. Among B, Al, Ga, and Tl, Tl (group 13, period 6) has the highest metallic character.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Arrange F, Cl, Br in order of decreasing electron gain enthalpy (most negative to least negative).

text_solutions: Electron gain enthalpy becomes less negative down group 17 due to increasing atomic size. Cl has the most negative value due to optimal nuclear charge and size, followed by F (less negative due to electron repulsion in its compact 2p orbitals), then Br. Order: Cl > F > Br.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Arrange the following elements in order of increasing covalent radius: N, P, As, Sb.

text_solutions: Covalent radius increases down group 15 due to additional electron shells. Order: N < P < As < Sb.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element forms a neutral oxide?

text_solutions: Neutral oxides do not react with acids or bases. C (group 14) forms \(\ce{CO}\), a neutral oxide, unlike \(\ce{Na2O}\) (basic), \(\ce{P2O5}\) (acidic), or \(\ce{Al2O3}\) (amphoteric).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide among the following is basic?

text_solutions: Basic oxides are formed by metals, especially s-block elements. \(\ce{BaO}\) (group 2) is basic, unlike \(\ce{N2O5}\) (acidic), \(\ce{SiO2}\) (acidic), or \(\ce{Al2O3}\) (amphoteric).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the smallest atomic radius among group 15 elements?

text_solutions: Atomic radius increases down a group. Among N, P, As, and Sb (group 15), N (period 2) has the smallest radius.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has a positive electron gain enthalpy?

text_solutions: Noble gases have positive electron gain enthalpies due to their stable configurations. Ne (group 18) requires energy to add an electron, unlike O, S, or Cl.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements exhibits variable valency due to d-orbital involvement?

text_solutions: d-block elements exhibit variable valency due to partially filled d-orbitals. Cu (group 11) shows this, unlike Na (s-block), Al (p-block), or Kr (p-block, full).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which d-block element in period 4 forms a compound with oxygen exhibiting the highest oxidation state of +7?

text_solutions: In period 4 d-block (Sc to Zn), Mn (group 7) achieves a +7 oxidation state in \(\ce{Mn2O7}\), unlike Cr (+6), Fe (+3), or Co (+3).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which pair of elements belongs to the same period?

text_solutions: Elements in the same period have the same principal quantum number. Na (3s¹) and Al (3p¹) are in period 3, unlike the other pairs spanning different periods.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 1 has the lowest first ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: First ionization enthalpy decreases down a group due to increased atomic size and shielding. Among Li, Na, K, and Cs, Cs (period 6) has the lowest value.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?

text_solutions: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group. Among Li, Be, N, and F, F (group 17, period 2) has the highest electronegativity due to its position on the far right of the periodic table.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the smallest ionic radius among the following cations?

text_solutions: For isoelectronic cations (\(\ce{Li+}\), \(\ce{Be^2+}\), \(\ce{B^3+}\), \(\ce{C^4+}\), all with 2 electrons), radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge. \(\ce{B^3+}\) (Z=5) is smaller than \(\ce{Li+}\) (Z=3), \(\ce{Be^2+}\) (Z=4), and \(\ce{C^4+}\) (Z=6).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element was predicted as Eka-aluminium by Mendeleev?

text_solutions: Mendeleev predicted Eka-aluminium below Al, later identified as Gallium (Ga), matching its properties like oxide formula \(\ce{Ga2O3}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide is neutral in nature?

text_solutions: Neutral oxides do not react with acids or bases. \(\ce{CO}\) (group 14) is neutral, unlike \(\ce{K2O}\) (basic), \(\ce{P2O5}\) (acidic), or \(\ce{ZnO}\) (amphoteric).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which pair of elements exhibits a diagonal relationship?

text_solutions: B (group 13, period 2) and Si (group 14, period 3) show a diagonal relationship due to similar size and properties, unlike the other pairs.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the general outer electronic configuration of group 16 elements?

text_solutions: Group 16 elements (chalcogens) have 6 valence electrons, with outer configuration \(ns^2 np^4\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the hydride formed by phosphorus?

text_solutions: P (group 15) forms \(\ce{PH3}\) with hydrogen, following the trend of group 15 hydrides.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element forms an oxide with the formula \(\ce{X2O}\), where X is a group 1 element?

text_solutions: Group 1 elements (except Li) form oxides of the type \(\ce{X2O}\). Rb, being in group 1, forms \(\ce{Rb2O}\), unlike Mg, Al, or P.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 13 has the highest tendency to form covalent compounds due to its polarizing power?

text_solutions: Polarizing power increases with smaller size and higher charge density. B³⁺ (smallest in group 13) has the highest tendency to form covalent compounds (e.g., \(\ce{BF3}\)) compared to Al, Ga, or In.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 13 element forms a hydride that is electron-deficient?

text_solutions: B forms \(\ce{B2H6}\), an electron-deficient hydride with three-center two-electron bonds, unlike Al (\(\ce{AlH3}\), polymeric), Ga, or In, which form less distinct hydrides.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Arrange the following elements in order of increasing first ionization enthalpy: B, C, N, O.

text_solutions: First ionization enthalpy generally increases across period 2, but N (half-filled \(2p^3\)) has higher stability than O. Order: B < C < O < N.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements has the highest first ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: First ionization enthalpy increases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge and decreases down a group due to increased shielding. Among Li, Be, Na, and Mg, Be (second period, group 2) has the highest value due to its stable \(2s^2\) configuration.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements is a halogen?

text_solutions: Halogens belong to group 17. Among O, S, Se, and Br, only Br is in group 17, making it a halogen.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Arrange the following ions in order of increasing ionic radius: \(\ce{F^-}\), \(\ce{Na+}\), \(\ce{Mg^2+}\).

text_solutions: For isoelectronic species (10 electrons), radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge: \(\ce{Mg^2+}\) (Z=12) < \(\ce{Na+}\) (Z=11) < \(\ce{F^-}\) (Z=9).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fourth period has the highest boiling point among d-block elements?

text_solutions: In period 4 d-block (Sc to Zn), boiling point peaks with strong metallic bonding. Cr (group 6) has the highest boiling point due to its \(3d^5 4s^1\) configuration and maximum unpaired electrons enhancing bonding.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fifth period has the highest second ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Second ionization enthalpy peaks when removing an electron from a stable \(\ce{X+}\) ion. Rb (after losing one electron, becomes \(\ce{Rb+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^6\)) has the highest value in period 5.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide is acidic in nature?

text_solutions: Oxides of non-metals (right side of periodic table) are acidic. \(\ce{SO3}\) (group 16) is acidic, while \(\ce{Na2O}\) (group 1), \(\ce{MgO}\) (group 2), and \(\ce{Al2O3}\) (group 13, amphoteric) are not purely acidic.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements forms a basic oxide?

text_solutions: Basic oxides are formed by metals, especially on the left side of the periodic table. K (group 1) forms \(\ce{K2O}\), a basic oxide, while C, S, and P form acidic or amphoteric oxides.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following carbonates has the highest thermal stability?

text_solutions: Thermal stability of group 1 carbonates increases down the group due to larger cation size stabilizing the lattice. \(\ce{Cs2CO3}\) is the most stable among Li, Na, K, and Cs carbonates.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the third period has the highest third ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Third ionization enthalpy peaks when removing an electron from a noble gas-like \(\ce{X^2+}\) ion. Mg (after losing two electrons, becomes \(\ce{Mg^2+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\)) has the highest value.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 18 has the largest atomic radius?

text_solutions: Atomic radius increases down a group. Among He, Ne, Ar, and Rn (group 18), Rn (period 6) has the largest radius.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: How many elements are present in the sixth period of the periodic table?

text_solutions: The sixth period (\(n=6\)) includes \(6s\), \(4f\), \(5d\), and \(6p\) orbitals, accommodating 32 electrons, hence 32 elements (Cs to Rn).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest second ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Second ionization enthalpy is highest when removing an electron from a stable configuration. Na (after losing one electron, becomes \(\ce{Na+}\) with noble gas configuration) has the highest value compared to Mg, Al, or Si.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 14 element forms a tetrachloride with the highest boiling point?

text_solutions: Boiling point of group 14 tetrachlorides (\(\ce{XCl4}\)) increases with molecular weight due to stronger London forces. \(\ce{SnCl4}\) (Sn, heaviest) has the highest boiling point among C, Si, Ge, and Sn.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which pair of elements from the same group shows the smallest difference in first ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: In group 13, Ga and In have a smaller ionization enthalpy difference due to d-block contraction effects, unlike B-Al, where the drop is larger due to a new shell.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide of a group 2 element is least soluble in water?

text_solutions: Solubility of group 2 oxides decreases down the group as lattice energy dominates over hydration energy. \(\ce{BaO}\) (largest cation) is the least soluble among BeO, MgO, CaO, and BaO.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a metalloid in group 14?

text_solutions: In group 14, Ge is a metalloid, while C (non-metal), Sn (metal), and Pb (metal) are not.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the largest ionic radius?

text_solutions: For isoelectronic species (\(\ce{N^3-}\), \(\ce{O^2-}\), \(\ce{F^-}\), \(\ce{Na+}\), all with 10 electrons), radius increases with decreasing nuclear charge. \(\ce{N^3-}\) (Z=7) has the largest radius.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which pair of elements from the same group shows the greatest increase in atomic radius?

text_solutions: Atomic radius increases down a group, with the largest jump often between early periods. In group 1, Li (period 2) to Na (period 3) shows a significant increase due to the addition of a new shell, compared to later pairs.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6\)?

text_solutions: Total electrons = 18, corresponding to Ar (period 3, group 18). Others: Cl (17 electrons), K (19 electrons), S (16 electrons).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which hydride is formed by a group 15 element?

text_solutions: Group 15 elements (N, P, As, etc.) form hydrides like \(\ce{NH3}\). \(\ce{CH4}\) (group 14), \(\ce{H2O}\) (group 16), and \(\ce{HCl}\) (group 17) are from other groups.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element belongs to the f-block of the periodic table?

text_solutions: f-block elements have electrons filling \(f\)-orbitals (lanthanoids and actinoids). Ce (Z=58) is an f-block element, while Sc (d-block), Rb (s-block), and Xe (p-block) are not.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a noble gas?

text_solutions: Noble gases (group 18) have a complete valence shell. Among He, Ne, Ar, and Kr, all are noble gases, but He is the simplest with \(1s^2\). Here, He is the correct choice based on options.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the highest second ionization enthalpy among the following?

text_solutions: Second ionization enthalpy is highest when removing an electron from a stable \(\ce{X+}\) ion. Li (becomes \(\ce{Li+}\) with \(1s^2\)) has the highest value compared to Be, B, or C.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the lowest atomic radius in the second period?

text_solutions: Atomic radius decreases across a period due to increasing nuclear charge. Among Li, B, N, and F, F (group 17, period 2) has the smallest radius.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a transition element?

text_solutions: Transition elements (d-block, groups 3–12) have partially filled d-orbitals. Fe (group 8) is a transition element, while Na (s-block), Al (p-block), and Cs (s-block) are not.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 14 element forms a monoxide with the highest bond strength?

text_solutions: Bond strength in group 14 monoxides (\(\ce{XO}\)) decreases down the group due to weaker orbital overlap. \(\ce{CO}\) (triple bond) has the highest bond strength compared to \(\ce{SiO}\), \(\ce{GeO}\), or \(\ce{SnO}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: How many elements are present in the f-block of the sixth period?

text_solutions: The f-block in period 6 corresponds to the lanthanoids (4f), with 14 elements (Ce to Lu).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide of a group 13 element is most resistant to hydrolysis?

text_solutions: \(\ce{B2O3}\) (covalent, network structure) is highly resistant to hydrolysis, unlike \(\ce{Al2O3}\) (amphoteric), \(\ce{Ga2O3}\), or \(\ce{In2O3}\), which react more readily with water or acids/bases.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 16 has the highest boiling point in its elemental form?

text_solutions: Boiling point increases down group 16 due to stronger intermolecular forces. Te (period 5, solid) has the highest boiling point among O₂, S₈, Se, and Te.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 13 element has the highest melting point due to its covalent network structure?

text_solutions: B (group 13) has a covalent network structure, giving it an exceptionally high melting point compared to Al, Ga, or In, which are metallic.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 13 element forms a trioxide with the highest acidity?

text_solutions: Acidity of group 13 trioxides decreases down the group. \(\ce{B2O3}\) (B, smallest) is the most acidic, forming boric acid, unlike \(\ce{Al2O3}\) (amphoteric), \(\ce{Ga2O3}\), or \(\ce{In2O3}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 14 element forms a dioxide with the lowest solubility in water?

text_solutions: Solubility of group 14 dioxides decreases down the group. \(\ce{SiO2}\) (network solid) has the lowest solubility compared to \(\ce{CO2}\) (forms \(\ce{H2CO3}\)), \(\ce{GeO2}\), or \(\ce{SnO2}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which ion among the following isoelectronic species with 18 electrons has the highest polarizing power?

text_solutions: For isoelectronic species (18 electrons), polarizing power increases with charge and decreases with size. \(\ce{Sc^3+}\) (Z=21, +3) has the highest polarizing power compared to \(\ce{K+}\), \(\ce{Ca^2+}\), or \(\ce{Cl^-}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fifth period d-block has the highest melting point?

text_solutions: In period 5 d-block (Y to Cd), melting point peaks with strong metallic bonding due to maximum unpaired electrons. Mo (group 6, \(4d^5 5s^1\)) has the highest melting point.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 15 element forms a trichloride with the highest covalent character?

text_solutions: Covalent character (Fajans’ rule) increases with smaller size and higher charge density. \(\ce{NCl3}\) (N, smallest) has the highest covalent character among N, P, As, and Sb trichlorides.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the IUPAC name of the element with atomic number 113?

text_solutions: Elements with \(Z > 100\) have systematic IUPAC names until officially named. For 113: 1 (un), 1 (un), 3 (tri) → ununtrium. However, it’s now officially Nihonium (Nh).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide of a group 14 element is predominantly covalent and acidic?

text_solutions: In group 14, \(\ce{CO2}\) (from C) is covalent and acidic, reacting with bases to form carbonates, unlike \(\ce{SiO2}\) (covalent but less acidic), \(\ce{GeO2}\), or \(\ce{SnO2}\) (amphoteric).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide of a fourth period element reacts with both acids and bases?

text_solutions: In period 4, \(\ce{ZnO}\) (from Zn, group 12) is amphoteric, reacting with acids (e.g., HCl) and bases (e.g., NaOH), unlike \(\ce{K2O}\) (basic), \(\ce{GeO2}\) (acidic), or \(\ce{As2O3}\) (acidic).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the general outer electronic configuration of group 1 elements?

text_solutions: Group 1 elements (alkali metals) have one valence electron, with outer configuration \(ns^1\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the maximum number of elements in the third period?

text_solutions: The third period (\(n=3\)) includes \(3s\) and \(3p\) orbitals, accommodating 8 electrons, hence 8 elements (Na to Ar).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the highest third ionization enthalpy among the following?

text_solutions: Third ionization enthalpy is highest when removing an electron from a noble gas-like configuration. Mg (after losing two electrons, becomes \(\ce{Mg^2+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\)) has the highest value.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the second period forms compounds with maximum covalency of 4?

text_solutions: Second period elements (Li to F) have only \(2s\) and \(2p\) orbitals, limiting covalency to 4. C (group 14) achieves this (e.g., \(\ce{CH4}\)), unlike Li, Be, or N.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements is a metalloid in group 15?

text_solutions: In group 15, As is a metalloid, while N (non-metal), P (non-metal), and Bi (metal) are not.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements is an alkaline earth metal?

text_solutions: Alkaline earth metals belong to group 2. Ca is in group 2, while B (group 13), N (group 15), and Cl (group 17) are not.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fourth period has the highest fifth ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Fifth ionization enthalpy peaks when removing an electron from a stable \(\ce{X^4+}\) ion. P (after losing four electrons, becomes \(\ce{P^4+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\)) has the highest value in period 4.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the electronic configuration ending in \(4s^2 4p^3\) in its ground state?

text_solutions: The configuration \(4s^2 4p^3\) corresponds to As (Z=33, period 4, group 15), with full configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^3\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 15 element forms a hydride with the highest bond angle?

text_solutions: Bond angles in group 15 hydrides (\(\ce{NH3}\), \(\ce{PH3}\), \(\ce{AsH3}\), \(\ce{SbH3}\)) decrease down the group due to reduced hybridization. \(\ce{NH3}\) (107°) has the highest bond angle.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Arrange O, S, Se in order of decreasing electronegativity.

text_solutions: Electronegativity decreases down a group due to increasing size. For group 16: O > S > Se.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following ions has the smallest radius among isoelectronic species with 18 electrons?

text_solutions: For isoelectronic species (\(\ce{K+}\), \(\ce{Ca^2+}\), \(\ce{Sc^3+}\), all with 18 electrons), radius decreases with increasing nuclear charge. \(\ce{Sc^3+}\) (Z=21) has the smallest radius.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a pnictogen?

text_solutions: Pnictogens are group 15 elements. Sb (group 15) is a pnictogen, while Te (group 16), I (group 17), and Sn (group 14) are not.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 14 element exhibits the maximum tendency to form \(\pi\)-bonds?

text_solutions: Smaller size and higher electronegativity favor \(\pi\)-bonding in group 14. C (period 2) forms \(\pi\)-bonds (e.g., in \(\ce{C2H4}\)) more readily than Si, Ge, or Sn due to effective 2p orbital overlap.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which pair of elements from different periods shows the least difference in electronegativity?

text_solutions: Diagonal relationships minimize electronegativity differences. Be (1.5, period 2) and Al (1.5, period 3) have nearly identical values, unlike other pairs with larger gaps.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following elements has the lowest melting point?

text_solutions: Melting point decreases down group 1 due to weaker metallic bonding. Cs (group 1, period 6) has the lowest melting point among Li, Na, and Cs.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which d-block element in period 5 has the highest electronegativity?

text_solutions: In period 5 d-block (Y to Cd), electronegativity increases across. Pd (group 10) has the highest electronegativity due to its position and nuclear charge.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the ground state electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^8 4s^2\)?

text_solutions: This configuration (Z=28) corresponds to Ni (period 4, group 10), with \(3d^8 4s^2\), distinguishing it from Fe (\(3d^6 4s^2\)), Co (\(3d^7 4s^2\)), or Cu (\(3d^{10} 4s^1\)).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 16 has the highest tendency to exhibit a +6 oxidation state?

text_solutions: The +6 oxidation state is most stable for S (e.g., in \(\ce{SO3}\)) due to its balance of size and electronegativity, unlike O, Se, or Te, where it’s less common or stable.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 15 element exhibits the maximum oxidation state of +5 in its compounds?

text_solutions: All group 15 elements can exhibit a +5 oxidation state, but N achieves it most prominently (e.g., in \(\ce{HNO3}\)) due to its small size and high electronegativity, unlike P, As, or Sb.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide of a group 17 element is the most stable in its highest oxidation state?

text_solutions: Stability of group 17 oxides in high oxidation states increases down the group. \(\ce{I2O5}\) (I, +5) is the most stable, unlike \(\ce{F2O}\), \(\ce{Cl2O7}\), or \(\ce{BrO3}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the ground state electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^5 4s^1\)?

text_solutions: This configuration (Z=24) corresponds to Cr, an exception due to the stability of half-filled \(3d^5\), unlike Mn (\(3d^5 4s^2\)), Fe (\(3d^6 4s^2\)), or Co (\(3d^7 4s^2\)).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which ion among the following isoelectronic species with 36 electrons has the highest lattice energy when paired with \(\ce{F^-}\)?

text_solutions: For isoelectronic species (36 electrons), lattice energy increases with charge. \(\ce{Sc^3+}\) (Z=21, +3) forms \(\ce{ScF3}\) with the highest lattice energy compared to \(\ce{K+}\), \(\ce{Ca^2+}\), or \(\ce{Br^-}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the highest first ionization enthalpy among group 13 elements?

text_solutions: First ionization enthalpy decreases down a group. Among B, Al, Ga, and Tl (group 13), B (period 2) has the highest value.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 14 has the highest ionization enthalpy after losing three electrons?

text_solutions: Fourth ionization enthalpy is highest for C (removing an electron from \(\ce{C^3+}\) with \(1s^2\)) due to its small size and stable configuration, compared to Si, Ge, or Sn.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the temporary systematic IUPAC name for the element with atomic number 115?

text_solutions: For \(Z = 115\): 1 (un), 1 (un), 5 (pent) → ununpentium (before its official name, Moscovium).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which d-block element in period 5 has the highest melting point?

text_solutions: In period 5 d-block (Y to Cd), melting point peaks with strong metallic bonding. Mo (group 6, \(4d^5 5s^1\)) has the highest melting point due to maximum unpaired electrons.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which pair of elements from the same period shows the greatest difference in electronegativity?

text_solutions: In period 2, the largest electronegativity difference is between Li (1.0) and F (4.0), a gap of 3.0, compared to other pairs like Be-B or C-N.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the temporary systematic name of the element with atomic number 115?

text_solutions: For \(Z=115\): 1 (un), 1 (un), 5 (pent) → ununpentium (before being named Moscovium).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 17 has the highest boiling point?

text_solutions: Boiling point increases down group 17 due to stronger London dispersion forces with larger size. I (period 5) has the highest boiling point among F, Cl, Br, and I.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the formula of the compound formed by aluminium and oxygen?

text_solutions: Al (group 13, valence 3) and O (group 16, valence 2) form \(\ce{Al2O3}\) by cross-multiplying valences.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 15 element forms a hydride with the lowest thermal stability?

text_solutions: Thermal stability of group 15 hydrides decreases down the group due to weaker X-H bonds. \(\ce{BiH3}\) (Bi, largest) has the lowest stability among \(\ce{NH3}\), \(\ce{PH3}\), \(\ce{AsH3}\), and \(\ce{BiH3}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest first ionization enthalpy among the third period elements?

text_solutions: First ionization enthalpy increases across a period. Among Na, Mg, Si, and Ar, Ar (group 18, period 3) has the highest value due to its stable noble gas configuration.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide is amphoteric in nature?

text_solutions: Amphoteric oxides, formed by elements near the metal-non-metal boundary, react with both acids and bases. \(\ce{As2O3}\) (group 15) is amphoteric, unlike \(\ce{Li2O}\) (basic), \(\ce{SO2}\) (acidic), or \(\ce{CO}\) (neutral).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following d-block elements in period 4 has an exceptional electronic configuration?

text_solutions: Cr (Z=24) has an exceptional configuration (\(3d^5 4s^1\)) due to the stability of a half-filled 3d subshell, unlike Sc (\(3d^1 4s^2\)), Mn (\(3d^5 4s^2\)), or Fe (\(3d^6 4s^2\)).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fifth period has the highest third ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Third ionization enthalpy peaks when removing an electron from a noble gas-like \(\ce{X^2+}\) ion. Sr (after losing two electrons, becomes \(\ce{Sr^2+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^6\)) has the highest value in period 5.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which d-block element in period 5 exhibits the highest oxidation state of +7?

text_solutions: In period 5 d-block (Y to Cd), Tc (group 7) achieves a +7 oxidation state (e.g., in \(\ce{Tc2O7}\)) due to the availability of d-electrons, unlike Zr, Nb, or Mo.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 14 element forms a dioxide with the highest bond energy?

text_solutions: Bond energy in \(\ce{XO2}\) decreases down group 14 due to weaker orbital overlap. \(\ce{CO2}\) (C=O) has the highest bond energy compared to \(\ce{SiO2}\), \(\ce{GeO2}\), or \(\ce{SnO2}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 15 has the lowest electronegativity?

text_solutions: Electronegativity decreases down group 15 due to increasing size. Bi (period 6) has the lowest value among N, P, As, and Bi.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which oxide of a group 15 element is the most acidic?

text_solutions: Acidity of group 15 oxides increases with oxidation state and decreases down the group. \(\ce{N2O5}\) (N in +5) is the most acidic, forming \(\ce{HNO3}\), unlike \(\ce{P2O5}\), \(\ce{As2O5}\), or \(\ce{Sb2O5}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fourth period has the highest fourth ionization enthalpy?

text_solutions: Fourth ionization enthalpy peaks when removing an electron from a stable \(\ce{X^3+}\) ion. Si (after losing three electrons, becomes \(\ce{Si^3+}\) with \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6\)) has the highest value.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a d-block element?

text_solutions: d-block elements (groups 3–12) have electrons filling d-orbitals. Mn (group 7) is a d-block element, while Ga (p-block), Rb (s-block), and Kr (p-block) are not.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in the subshells filled in the fifth period?

text_solutions: The fifth period (\(n=5\)) includes \(5s\) (2 electrons), \(4d\) (10 electrons), and \(5p\) (6 electrons), totaling 18 electrons.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 16 element forms a trioxide with the highest oxidation state?

text_solutions: Group 16 trioxides (\(\ce{XO3}\)) show a +6 oxidation state. S forms \(\ce{SO3}\), the most stable and common trioxide, unlike O, Se, or Te where \(\ce{XO3}\) is less prevalent.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: What is the general outer electronic configuration of d-block elements?

text_solutions: d-block elements (groups 3–12) have electrons filling \((n-1)d\) orbitals, with outer configuration \((n-1)d^{1-10} ns^{0-2}\).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 2 element forms a hydroxide with the lowest solubility in water?

text_solutions: Solubility of group 2 hydroxides increases down the group due to decreasing lattice energy. \(\ce{Be(OH)2}\) has the lowest solubility due to Be’s small size and high charge density.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following fluorides has the highest ionic character?

text_solutions: Ionic character increases with larger cation size and lower polarizing power in group 2. \(\ce{BaF2}\) (Ba²⁺, largest) has the highest ionic character among BeF₂, MgF₂, CaF₂, and BaF₂.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Arrange the following elements in order of increasing metallic character: Si, P, S, Cl.

text_solutions: Metallic character decreases across period 3 due to increasing nuclear charge. Order: Cl < S < P < Si.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which group 17 element has the highest electron affinity despite not having the most negative electron gain enthalpy?

text_solutions: Electron affinity is the energy change for \(\ce{X + e^- -> X^-}\). Cl has the highest electron affinity due to its balance of size and nuclear charge, though F’s electron gain enthalpy is less negative due to repulsion.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following has the highest lattice energy among group 2 fluorides?

text_solutions: Lattice energy increases with smaller ionic radii (higher charge density). BeF₂ has the highest lattice energy in group 2 due to Be²⁺’s small size, compared to MgF₂, CaF₂, or SrF₂.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element has the electronic configuration \(1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^1\)?

text_solutions: Total electrons = 11, corresponding to Na (period 3, group 1). Others: Mg (12 electrons), Al (13 electrons), Ne (10 electrons).

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in the fourth period has the highest electronegativity?

text_solutions: Electronegativity increases across a period. In period 4 (K to Kr), Br (group 17) has the highest electronegativity among K, Ca, and Br.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 16 has the most negative electron gain enthalpy?

text_solutions: Electron gain enthalpy becomes more negative across a period and less negative down a group. In group 16, O (period 2) has the most negative value compared to S, Se, and Te.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which element in group 15 has the highest tendency to form stable compounds in the +3 oxidation state?

text_solutions: The +3 oxidation state becomes more stable down group 15 due to the inert pair effect. Bi forms stable \(\ce{BiCl3}\) (+3), more so than N, P, or As, where +5 is also common.

questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

qns_content.text: Which of the following is a chalcogen?

text_solutions: Chalcogens are group 16 elements. Te (group 16) is a chalcogen, while As (group 15), Br (group 17), and Ge (group 14) are not.
